## Overview: Why No Single Simulation Answers Every Empirical Question

Across the stepwise tutorials (Part II), spatial workflows (Part III), and methodological deep dives (Part IV), every core component of `medusa` is paired with numerical checks and Monte Carlo simulations. A thoughtful investigator or peer reviewer should still ask a sharper meta-question:

*Which properties of MEDuSA are guaranteed by linear algebra, which depend on empirical regularity conditions tested in Monte Carlo benchmarks, and how can I verify that my own study's event schedule, motion censoring, and sample size support calibrated inference before testing substantive hypotheses?*

::: {.callout-note}
### Core Methodological Question & Connection to the Pipeline
*Where do general package benchmarks end and study-specific design geometry begin—and how do you turn an empirical `events` table and `valid_rows` mask from [Step 0](medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd) into a custom end-to-end calibration check?*

This capstone chapter synthesizes the evidence across all four Part IV deep dives and the [14-Study Validation Suite](library/medusa_validation_suite.html), then provides a compact R template for study-specific synthetic calibration.
:::

---

## 1. Three Distinct Layers of Evidence in `medusa`

Keeping three levels of validation distinct prevents both over-claiming and unnecessary skepticism:

1. **Exact conditional operator identities (algebraic & numerical checks):** Once run $r$'s HRF, smoothing parameter $\lambda_v$, adaptive weights, and noise correlation $\Sigma_{\text{cor}}$ are fixed, deconvolution ($D_r$) and de-mixed epoch readout ($B_{r,\tau}$) are deterministic linear maps. Identities such as $\operatorname{Cov}(B_{r,\tau}\varepsilon_r) = \sigma_{\text{obs}}^2 B_{r,\tau}\Sigma_{\text{cor}}B_{r,\tau}^\top$ ([Propagating BOLD Noise into Trial SEs](medusa_standard_errors_mmom.qmd)), scale invariance under `restore_scale = TRUE`, and $B_g G_g = I$ in full-rank finite bases ([Latent Connectivity Beyond Per-Trial Disattenuation](medusa_connectivity_inference/medusa_connectivity_inference.qmd)) hold to machine precision ($10^{-13}\text{--}10^{-15}$). They guarantee that the code computes the exact mathematical quantity promised—*conditional* on the first-stage operators.
2. **Isolated mechanism stress tests (Part IV deep dives & chapter benchmarks):** Each mechanism study varies one realistic threat at a time while holding surrounding structure transparent—such as fast/slow neurovascular dispersion against $\text{AR}(3)$ noise ([Autocorrelation Prewhitening Under Fast-TR Event Designs](medusa_step1_hrf_noise/woolrich_review/woolrich_noise_assessment.qmd)), censored edge lags and serial trial dependence in `medusa_multilag_infer()` ([Simultaneous Bands Across Lags](medusa_multilag_calibration/medusa_multilag_calibration.qmd)), or unequal regional smoothing $K_S \neq K_T$ and small-$S$ clustering in connectivity ([Latent Connectivity Beyond Per-Trial Disattenuation](medusa_connectivity_inference/medusa_connectivity_inference.qmd)). These isolate *why* an estimator succeeds or breaks down.
3. **End-to-end pipeline Monte Carlo benchmarks ([14-Study Validation Suite](library/medusa_validation_suite.html)):** Refits the entire sequence (`estimate_crossrun_hrf()` $\to$ `deconvolve_crossrun_hrf()` $\to$ `decon_epoch_regression()` $\to$ `mixed_by()` / `medusa_multilag_infer()` / `decon_connectivity_repair()`) inside every synthetic cohort, capturing how estimation uncertainty in Step 1 HRF selection and Step 2 GCV/RWLS tuning propagates into final population $p$-values and confidence intervals.

## 2. Synthesis Map: Claims Tested vs. Scope Boundaries

| Evidence source | Primary pipeline claim evaluated | Key scope boundary to check in your study |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **[Autocorrelation Prewhitening](medusa_step1_hrf_noise/woolrich_review/woolrich_noise_assessment.qmd)** & Validation Study 12 | Two-pass target-excluding REML $\text{AR}(p)$ refit + Winsorized GLS `noise_sd` recovers true ACF and full trial covariance $\Omega_{r,\tau}$ (`4–8%` Frobenius error vs. `21–28%` under single-pass canonical HRF) | Requires $R \ge 2$ runs (recommended $R \ge 3$) and drift/motion confounds modeled so $\widehat{\rho}$ is not pinned at `0.90`; use `pooling = "graph"` when parcels cross pial/CSF borders. |
| **[Propagating BOLD Noise into Trial SEs](medusa_standard_errors_mmom.qmd)** & Validation Studies 1–4 | Operator-propagated `se_demixed`, `(1 - 1/m)^{-1}` run-centering calibration, and `precision_weight_cohort` improve group slope RMSE and maintain nominal mixed-model Type I error | Treats first-stage `se_demixed^2` as fixed plug-in variances; requires centering within-person covariates (`x_within`) and specifying participant random slopes in `mixed_by()`. |
| **[Step 1–3](medusa_step2_deconvolution/medusa_step2_deconvolution.qmd)** & Validation Studies 5–9, 13–14 | 3D physiological HRF library (`preset = "medusa"`, `normalize = "positive_lobe"`), monotone SNR-stratified `lambda_mode = "auto"`, `rwls = "auto"` glitch protection, and `(T, O)` epoch demixing | Sub-second fixed ISIs without inter-phase jitter remain fundamentally collinear under hemodynamic low-pass filtering (audit via [Step 0](medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd) and `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()`). |
| **[Simultaneous Bands Across Lags](medusa_multilag_calibration/medusa_multilag_calibration.qmd)** & Validation Study 11 | Studentized Wishart draws + available-case lag pooling hold `Max-|T|`, `1D TFCE`, `omnibus_p`, and `"unsmoothed"` window contrasts near nominal 5% / 95% targets under serial dependence and missing participant edge lags | `p_maxT` and `p_tfce` control FWER across lags of *one* `(parcel, term)` curve; apply `"holm"` or `"BY"` across `omnibus_p` when testing multiple parcels. |
| **[Latent Connectivity](medusa_connectivity_inference/medusa_connectivity_inference.qmd)**, **[Step 6](medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd)**, & Validation Study 10 | Per-trial M-MOMS + Adaptive-POET & dynamic covariance regression (`shared_error_method = "poet_covreg"`, `shared_error = "auto"`, `variance_confounds`) + `crosstrial_se = TRUE` ($N=1$ Satterthwaite SEs & cohort HKSJ $t$-intervals) remove predictor attenuation plus stationary and multi-parcel/confound-driven dynamic shared noise | Pairwise-only condition-flipped noise lacking both a multi-parcel factor signature and a measured `variance_confounds` envelope—or severe seed–target smoothing mismatch ($K_S \neq K_T$)—still requires a [shared-error sensitivity curve](medusa_step6_connectivity/medusa_step6_connectivity.qmd#fig-sensitivity) and matched Step 2–3 demixing. |

## 3. Building a Study-Specific Calibration on Your Own Schedule

Whenever an empirical study uses a novel multi-phase trial timing, heavy motion scrubbing, or small cohort size, the most informative validation you can run is a **synthetic twin of your exact task geometry**. Because `read_fmriprep_subject()` ([Step 0](medusa_step0_design_bids/medusa_step0_design_bids.qmd)) already extracts each participant's real `events` table, run lengths, `TR`, and framewise-displacement `valid_rows` masks, you can simulate synthetic BOLD directly on top of your actual empirical design in ~35 lines of R—*without* peeking at real neural associations:

1. **Lock the estimand and multiplicity rule upfront:** Prespecify the target condition, peri-event lag(s), covariates, window contrasts, and parcel-family adjustment (`"holm"` or `"BY"`).
2. **Keep real onset times, durations, and censor masks intact:** Use your cohort's actual `events` timestamps, reaction-time durations, and `valid_rows` scrubbing vectors so collinearity between adjacent task phases and run-end/motion truncation match your study verbatim.
3. **Include both an active parcel and a structured null parcel:** Generate voxelwise HRF dispersion from `hrf_library()`, realistic $\text{AR}(1)$ temporal noise ($\rho \approx 0.45\text{--}0.60$), and—if testing Step 6 PPI—shared cross-parcel background innovations.
4. **Refit the full `medusa` pipeline in every replicate:** Run `estimate_crossrun_hrf()`, `deconvolve_crossrun_hrf()`, and `decon_epoch_regression()` from scratch inside the loop rather than freezing oracle HRFs or smoothing parameters.
5. **Audit bias, CI coverage, null false positives, and gating rates together:** Check `mean(is.na(decon_demixed))`, `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()$summary$mean_gain`, `isSingular()` rates in `mixed_by()`, and empirical 95% coverage.

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
library(medusa)

# Template: Synthetic twin check on one participant's real empirical schedule & scrub mask
# Assumes `sub01` was loaded via read_fmriprep_subject() in Step 0
tr   <- sub01$tr
cand <- hrf_library(tr = tr, preset = "medusa")
evs  <- split(sub01$events, sub01$events$run)
vrows <- lapply(sub01$confounds$runs, `[[`, "valid_rows")

sim_one_subject <- function(beta_true = 0.40, noise_sd = 0.35, rho = 0.50) {
  parcels <- setNames(rep(c("Active_ROI", "Null_ROI"), each = 6L), paste0("v", 1:12))
  h_act   <- cand[, sample(ncol(cand), 1L)]   # random physiological HRF draw
  h_null  <- cand[, sample(ncol(cand), 1L)]
  bold_sim <- cov_sim <- list()

  for (r in names(evs)) {
    n_t <- nrow(sub01$bold[[r]])
    ev  <- evs[[r]]
    t_idx <- which(ev$condition == "feedback")
    x_mod <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(length(t_idx))))

    # Forward neural impulse series on the real empirical timestamps
    s_act <- s_null <- numeric(n_t)
    grid_t <- (0:(n_t - 1L)) * tr
    for (j in seq_along(t_idx)) {
      imp <- pmax(0, 1 - abs(grid_t / tr - ev$onset[t_idx[j]] / tr))
      s_act  <- s_act  + imp * (1.0 + beta_true * x_mod[j])
      s_null <- s_null + imp * 1.0            # evoked response, zero modulator slope
    }
    y_act  <- as.numeric(stats::convolve(s_act,  rev(h_act),  type = "open"))[seq_len(n_t)]
    y_null <- as.numeric(stats::convolve(s_null, rev(h_null), type = "open"))[seq_len(n_t)]

    ar_draw <- function() as.numeric(stats::arima.sim(list(ar = rho), n = n_t, sd = noise_sd * sqrt(1 - rho^2)))
    Y <- cbind(
      replicate(6L, 100 + y_act  + ar_draw()),
      replicate(6L, 100 + y_null + ar_draw())
    )
    colnames(Y) <- names(parcels)
    bold_sim[[r]] <- Y
    cov_sim[[r]]  <- data.frame(x_within = x_mod)
  }

  hf <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(bold_sim, evs, tr = tr, kernel_grid = cand,
                              valid_rows = vrows, spatial_groups = parcels, pooling = "parcel")
  dc <- deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(bold_sim, hf, scaling = "noise_sd", penalty = "sobolev")
  decon_epoch_regression(dc, cov_sim, evs, target_condition = "feedback",
                         lags = 0, parcel_groups = parcels, restore_scale = TRUE, return_panel = TRUE)
}
```

Looping `sim_one_subject()` across your cohort's `sub01..subN` schedules and feeding the resulting panels into `mixed_by()` (or `decon_connectivity_repair()`) gives an exact, pre-data answer to whether your task jitter, run count, and motion censoring support unbiased slope recovery and nominal 5% false-positive control in `Null_ROI`.
